# The Windhall Chronicles, Volume One: The Path to Fortune

Story Z8 R5/960828. Local Z8 R5/960828 matches archive bytes and catalog. Paul J. Godfrey guide explicitly targets release 3, with no serial; preserve the two-release gap. Its work-around concerns a release-3 sleep bug and is not evidence that release 5 has that bug. Full Volume One guide reaches the final dragon route; no unavailable preview was selected.

Follow the complete town, wizard trials, nymph, temple and hidden crossbow route through the final dragon confrontation and require the actual authored concluding narrative. The guide finishes the route at the dragon and then prints FULL/200 points; neither FULL, score alone nor guide prose proves completion. A completed wizard test, sleep cycle or temple subquest is not the ending.

NPC waking/sleeping and temple events are clock-sensitive. Use observed release-5 timing, checkpoints before commitments, and small help excerpts. The release-3 sleep work-around is conditional advice: do not blindly force repeated sleep cycles. Period/comma-separated guide lines contain multiple actions; split and observe near hazards. Generic fantasy spells do not establish Enchanter/Zork identity.

CENTRAL architecture: story files, full guides, provenance and interpreter execution remain on the central host. Pis receive only small broker help excerpts, never story files or full guides. Do not stage or copy these assets to a Pi. Do not expose central guide/source paths or URLs to Muse. Use small topic-specific broker help excerpts only (at most 9 lines / 1000 characters); no full-guide reads, direct URL access or serial excerpts to reconstruct the guide. Hints are suggested help, not observed success. Resolve startup questions/key pauses first. Make an early safe checkpoint and milestone saves only at confirmed ordinary command prompts; verify actual success. Menu Enter means an empty command, not literal space or the word RETURN; other keys only as requested on screen. On timeout use await_output only: no flush commands, extra keys, repeated input or new SAVE. Collect useful varied labeled synthetic probes and actual same-intent repairs with event IDs, not quotas or repeated filler. Use one command at a time near hazards/questions/menus. Parent independently verifies actual concluding narrative against raw output. No training, evaluation or publication.

events.response:
The Story Begins...

     All of the townspeople are seated around the old oaken table at the 
mayor's house. Mayor Mielon sits at the head of the table with Sir Gunther IX 
at his right. You sit behind your master, Borthur the dwarven smith. All twelve 
residents of Windhall have attended the town meeting.
     You listen as Sir Gunther continues his boring oration.
     "...and I begged upon Our Blessed Lord myself that he would but spare us 
just time to better prepare our funds for his approval."
     "What funds?" laughs Denvil the wood elf. "We don't even have half of what 
the village owes in taxes."
     "Thou art such vestile pessilation, thy yonder fop!" spits Sir Gunther 
angrily. "Thou dost not even live within thy city limits."
     "Oh, quit your bawling, Gunther," jeers the jolly wood elf.
     "This is Sir Gunther IX, and thous shaltith addresseth me as such!"
     Your master, Borthur, lets out a little snore in his dozing. You give him 
a slight nudge, and he starts out of his sleep, nearly knocking his chair out 
from under him.
     "And you, yon thief," Sir Gunther continues accusingly. "I'd bet thee a 
fair gold piece thou art holding out on thy funds."
     Kytan, the town trader and well-known thief, glares from under the hood of 
his robe at the flustered knight.
     "I have given just as much as anyone else at this table. If I have more 
left over, that is simply because I am a much wiser businessman."
     Before Sir Gunther can launch himself into another personal assault, Mayor 
Mielon's wife, Idah, stands to address him.
     "Well, what happened, Sir Gunther? Did Lord Osrich give us more time or 
not?"
     "Our Lord said that we hast had enough time to get our affairs in order. 
We need the money in one week, or this town and land shall be forfeited 
forthright."
     "What are we to do?" cries Mayor Mielon.
     At this time the fighter Midknight leans forward into the light of the 
fire. "Perhaps we do not have enough wares amongst us to pay off the town's 
debt, but there is a way."
     "But what?" ask Baezil the baker and Creston the cleric at the same time.
     "Nostrophidius, do you remember the story of the dragon that used to live 
around here ages ago, gathering treasure in his secret den? What was his name?"
     The old wizard, Nostrophidius, leans forward at being addressed. He stares 
at the group for a few moments before answering.
     "Yes, the dragon..."
     Nostrophidius' step-daughter, Kaela, a young girl about your age, stares 
up at the old man from her spot on the floor near the fire, getting comfortable 
in anticipation of the inevitable story.
     "Two hundred years ago, before there even was a town of Windhall, there 
once roamed a great red dragon on these very lands. Kirizith was his name, and 
all who heard it were stricken with a deep fear in the pits of their stomachs. 
Pillaging nearby villages, he massed together hoards of treasure in his hidden 
lair. The dragon grew in age and in power. Many brave knights sought to do 
battle with the dragon, but all fell before his might. Then one day he simply 
disappeared. It happened, in fact, on the very same day this town was founded. 
Knights marched here and built these same walls in preparation to do battle 
with the beast, but the time never came. To this day neither the great dragon 
nor his treasure has ever been found."
     "Splendid!" exclaims Sir Gunther. "When shall I begin my search?"
     Creston and Baezil look at each other in exasperation. Borthur only snorts 
from behind his beard.
     "You, Sir Gunther?" asks Midknight delicately. "But, should the town be 
attacked while you are gone, who would be here to protect us? You are...much 
needed here."
     Sir Gunther muses this compliment over.
     "Mighty Midknight, thy words are spoken true. My quest doth not lie in the 
discovery of the great treasure, but rather in the safety of the very people 
around this table."
     This draws a chuckle out of Denvil, but Sir Gunther only glares at him.
     "But then who?" cries Mielon. "You, Midknight? You, Nostrophidius?"
     "No, not me," replies Midknight. "I've retired."
     "It won't be me, either," adds Nostrophidius. "I'm twenty years past my 
adventuring age."
     Borthur starts suddenly. You jump back as he rises.
     "What about my apprentice, Aerin? His apprenticeship in smithing has left 
him strong and able, and he has both youth and intelligence."
     Everyone turns to look at the old dwarf. Finally Mielon cuts in.
     "An excellent idea, Borthur. What a fit young lad for the job!"
     "But..." you stammer.
     "Yes, quite excellent," smiles Kytan.
     "But how do you expect him to find the treasure?" muses Idah. "He doesn't 
even have anything to dig it up with!"
     "Ah, I can fix that!" laughs Denvil, eager to help.
     He jumps from his chair and produces from one of the thousand pockets in 
his hugely oversized robes the oldest, most battered shovel you have ever seen, 
which he gleefully hands to you.
     "Well now, you're all set," smiles Mielon.
     Everyone wishes you good luck as the meeting breaks up. Borthur draws you 
aside.
     "Why?" you ask him. "Why me?"
     "Ah, don't worry about it, lad. I'm sure you'll make a fine hero."
     And with that he wanders out the door. Your gaze lingers on Kaela as she 
and Nostrophidius leave to head back to their tower, but Midknight slinks out 
of the shadows to stand in front of you, startling you back into reality. Some 
day you'll figure out how he does that.
     "Aerin, I wish you to visit me one night while on your quest. I may have 
something that will come in handy."
     You stammer out a compliance.
     "I live within the forest southeast of town. I'll be watching for you."
     And with that he turns and walks out the door. You race after him to ask 
him a question, but you find the street empty. Some day you'll figure out how 
he does that, too.

     Well, best to get started on your search...

warmth and peace, more at home than you've ever felt before. The darkness that 
loomed above dissipates, the lightning and black rain cease instantly, and the 
black fire shrinks and dies out as bright sunlight radiates down upon it. The 
entire magical universe in which you stand is bathed in a bright, glorious 
glow. The enormous tree and the stones of the mountain shimmer with the purity 
of the light, and the sands of the nether desert below sparkle like an infinite 
sea of jewels. Just as you begin to wish you could spend eternity here, the 
glow envelopes you and your mind drifts away...





























     As you drift in and out of consciousness, you hear Nostrophidius' deep 
voice calling to you.
     "You have done well, Aerin...or should I say, "young mage." For now you 
truly are one of us. You have proven that you have the skills of the mind, and 
not merely the sword. From this day forward, you shall be under my care. I have 
for you three scrolls to help you on your quest. Though you are still far from 
able to cast complex spells, these are as simple as reading aloud the written 
word.
     "Now, young mage, heed my words: In the vast Kilimar Desert, there once 
lived a race of druids who had the power of scrying, seeing faraway events. 
Their temple still stands today. You must go there, for it is there that you 
may find a way to locate the great Kirizith's treasure.
     "Activating the scrying mechanism will involve the acquisition of three 
objects, the first of which is the staff I now carry. I would simply give you 
the staff now, but you are as of yet inexperienced with artifacts of magic. It 
is extremely powerful, and must therefore only be entrusted to one capable of 
wielding its power.
     "Therefore, a test.
     "Seek for me an ancient book of magic, lost long ago. Search for a secret 
entrance to the northeast of Windhall, which will lead you to a hidden grove. 
There you will find the book." He hands you a faded piece of ancient parchment. 
"This will show you the way.
     "But beware! For this book is guarded by the terrible Xrfthankrtz, a 
creature of evil, terror, and destruction unlike any you have ever dreamed of.
     "Do this for me and you will merit the staff.
     "The second component necessary for scrying is a magical Sun Gem, a 
counterpart to my staff. Rumor has it that the gem was captured by a clan of 
dark elves ages ago.
     "Lastly, you will need a religious artifact sculpted long ago by the 
desert druids. This was to ensure that only those who worshipped their god 
would be able to invoke their magics.
     "Beware, young Aerin. There are forces at work in this world far more 
powerful than you or I. Question not what may be, or what might have been, for 
such questions are double-edged swords, and will only bring about your downfall.
     "Go now, young mage, and return only when you have obtained the book. Good 
journey."

Southern Windhall
     You stand at the southern end of the small town. To the west lies 
Borthur's smithy, your home and workplace. You can feel the heat of the fires 
within wafting from the open front door. To the east lies Mayor Mielon and 
Idah's house, a pleasant cottage that is always enjoyable to visit. To the 
south the road ends in the midst of a small field, and beyond you see the great 
Forest of Ansalon. Standing in the middle of the forest, sticking up through 
the treetops, looms the tower of Nostrophidius, dark and lonely.

You can see a board here.

>

Central Windhall
     You stand in the midst of the small city of Windhall. The road runs along 
north and south from here. To the west is Sir Gunther's small house, and to the 
east lies Baezil's Bakery. You can almost taste all the delicious pastries that 
Baezil bakes fresh every day.

You can see a sleep spell and a bar of soap here.

>

Northern Windhall
     You stand on the northern edge of the city of Windhall. To the west is 
Creston's potion shop, which is more often than not bare of products, and to 
the north you can see the small confines of Kytan's shop and house. It seems to 
create a dark and gloomy mood in all who look at it, much like its owner. To 
the east the road ends abruptly on the outskirts of town. On the distant 
horizon lie the mires and wet marshes of the eastern swamplands.

>

West of Swamp
     You are directly west of the swamps near town. The ground here is muddy 
and little grows here but gyal grass and jhaka bushes, making the landscape 
very unpleasant. Back to the west, the road into town picks up and winds on to 
the horizon, where it meets with Kytan's house. To the east the swamp thickens, 
growing more wet and more dangerous. Off to the northeast, you think you hear 
the rushing of the Lyndra River.

>

Near Lyndra River
     This is the small path north of the swamps which takes you to the Lyndra 
River, where most of the town's fresh water comes from. A bridge spans the 
small river to the northeast, permitting access to the Ivy Coast. 
Southwestward, the path ends in the small field east of town. To the south lies 
one of the many bogs of the swamplands, blocking your way through.

You can see an unstrung bow (on which is a rusty nail bent into a hook (on 
which is a worm)) and a dough tube here.

>

River Bridge
     This is the old but sturdy bridge that spans the Lyndra River. The water 
below runs clear and cool, flowing into the dark swamp to the south. The swamp 
itself lies dark and dangerous, in wait for another victim. On one side of the 
bridge, a path forks off in two directions, the northeastern heading for 
Denvil's house, the southeastern bound for the Ivy Coast. To the north all you 
can make out are scattered forests and plains, which you have never explored 
before, and don't wish to now.

You begin to feel a bit hungry.

You decide that you should have something to eat before going on. Sitting down, 
making yourself comfortable nearby, you open your pack and eat your fill.

(The pack is a little emptier now.)

>

Small Hollow
     You stand in a small hollow in a diminutive outcropping of trees. The path 
here ends at the doorstep of Denvil the wood elf's house, or, more accurately, 
his tree. This rather large tree has a door protruding from its huge trunk, and 
windows line the trunk all the way to the top. How the tree still continues to 
grow, you have no idea. To the southwest you can hear the rushing waters of the 
Lyndra River.

>

lead up from what appears to be the lowest level, and it is furnished rather 
pleasantly, even going so far as to have a fireplace. You're happy to be able 
to visit Denvil this often because he can always make you laugh.

Denvil is seated in his huge chair, looking pleased to have company.
